description:
🚀 AIDeep Economics | AI, Earth Observation & Climate-Resilient Agriculture

We are a multidisciplinary team from AIDeep Economics, a Uruguayan AgTech company specializing in artificial intelligence, satellite remote sensing, geospatial analytics, and agricultural decision-support systems.

Our team combines expertise in agronomy, environmental science, soil conservation, hydrology, biophysical modeling, software engineering, and AI.
summary:
🌍 Climate change has shattered the “average year” in rainfed agriculture.

Across Uruguay and global breadbaskets, farmers swing violently between:

🏜️ Historic droughts, which recently cost Uruguay over USD 1.17 billion.

🌧️ Extreme Super El Niño downpours that strip away decades of fertile topsoil during bare-soil windows.

Choosing a multi-year crop rotation is now a high-stakes balancing act: winter cover crops shield soil from storms, yet draw down stored moisture needed by summer harvests. 

🛰️ Field Shift Rotation Twin: An End-to-End Digital Twin for Farm Rotations

The platform combines NASA satellite observations, geospatial foundation models, and local soil profiles to evaluate rotations across:

Historical Super El Niño and drought extremes.

Synthetic storms and seasonal forecasts.

Climate projections

🌱 Coupled Biophysical & Economic Simulation

Integrated engines simulate:

Soil and water: Erosion, root-zone water, and soil carbon.

Crop vulnerability: Flowering risk.

Farm economics: Multi-year cash flows, grain-and-livestock margins, and price tipping points.

🎯 Decisions That Account for Uncertainty

Multi-objective optimization balances competing priorities.

Robust decision rules abstain when uncertainty is too high.

Per-hectare valuation identifies what to measure first.

🏛️ From Farm Planning to National Verification

Field Shift automates Uruguay’s mandatory Soil Use Plans for farmers and national compliance verification for regulators.
details:
🌍 The Problem: Farming Between Billion-Dollar Droughts and Super El Niño Storms

Rainfed agriculture no longer operates in a stable “average” climate. Intensifying climate change is driving severe hydroclimatic whiplash across South America and global food-producing regions:

  • 🏜️ Devastating multi-year droughts: Uruguay’s 2022–2023 water crisis caused over USD 1.175 billion in direct agricultural losses.
  • 🌧️ Violent Super El Niño storm regimes: Concentrated downpours strike bare ground and wash away decades of fertile topsoil in days.

Every multi-year crop rotation forces an agronomic and financial trade-off across time:

  • Winter cover crops and pastures protect soil during peak storm months and build organic matter, yet consume stored root-zone moisture needed by summer cash crops if spring rains fail.
  • Winter fallow preserves moisture on paper, yet exposes fragile topsoil when Super El Niño deluges hit hardest.

Despite this volatility, conventional conservation workflows still evaluate farms one scenario at a time, under static long-term climate averages that conceal financial and physical fragility.

🛰️ What Field Shift Rotation Twin Does: Six Coupled Layers from Space to Farm Cash Flow

Field Shift Rotation Twin is an open-source spatial digital twin and decision-support platform organized across six integrated layers.

① 📍 Multi-Field Mapping, Satellite Observation & Crop-History Reconstruction

Through the interactive field workbench (#/fields), producers:

  • Map or select farm fields.
  • Preload local site properties: Soil units, pedotransfer hydraulic properties, erodibility, legal soil-loss tolerances, and topographic slope.
  • Reconstruct crop history and dry residue cover under human review, using multi-sensor Earth observations and geospatial foundation-model proposals.

Earth observation sources: HLS harmonized Landsat and Sentinel-2, MODIS, EMIT hyperspectral fractional cover, and SRTM / NASADEM.

Foundation-model proposals: Prithvi-EO-2.0, Galileo, and Presto.

② 💧 Surface-to-Root Soil Moisture & Evapotranspiration Assimilation

Combines complementary observations through an Ensemble Kalman Filter (EnKF):

  • Regional moisture context: SMAP L4.
  • Surface moisture inversion: Sentinel-1 + Sentinel-2 Water Cloud Model (S²MP / WCM).
  • L-band moisture: NISAR.
  • Thermal evapotranspiration: ECOSTRESS.

Assimilation uses explicit observation operators, holdout splits, and error bounds.

③ 🌦️ Three-Horizon Climate Simulation Engine

The platform keeps past extremes, next-season forecasts, and future projections strictly separated.

Historical Records & Synthetic Extremes

  • Multi-decade daily NASA POWER and GPM IMERG series.
  • Classification of historical Super El Niño deluges, neutral years, and La Niña droughts, using NOAA ONI v6.
  • Intensified-rainfall stress tests.
  • A stochastic Markov weather generator for compound extremes beyond the instrumental record.

Tactical Next-Season Ensembles

  • Sub-seasonal and seasonal forecasts from NASA GEOS-S2S-3 and NMME.
  • Support for timing in-season cover-crop termination ahead of incoming wet or dry anomalies.

2030–2060 Climate-Change Projections

  • Downscaled daily NASA NEX-GDDP-CMIP6 scenarios.
  • Direct comparison with ISIMIP3b multi-model ensembles.
  • Cross-model scenario agreement, preserving ensemble differences rather than collapsing them into a single average.

④ 🌱 Coupled Biophysical Twin & Flowering-Window Risk

The engine chains daily state continuously across decades, without seasonal resets.

Soil Erosion

  • Long-term normative conservation pre-evaluation: RUSLE / EROSION 6.0 against soil tolerance T.
  • Exploratory storm analysis: Storm-by-storm, 30-minute IMERG EI30 erosivity.
  • Landscape transport: Topographic flow routing and Borselli sediment connectivity.

Water, Thermal Phenology & Yield

  • Two Monthly NASA Climate Clocks: Erosive rainfall share versus atmospheric water demand.
  • Continuous daily root-zone water balance: FAO-56 Penman–Monteith with dual crop coefficients.
  • Runoff and evaporation: USDA Curve Number runoff and surface evaporation under residue.
  • Thermal exposure: Monthly frost and heat-stress counts.
  • Flowering and sowing risk: Calibrated thermal-photoperiod flowering phenology (WOFOST-class) and multi-year sowing-window risk sweeps.
  • Water-limited yield comparisons: FAO-33 Ky and AquaCrop-OSPy.

Residues & Multi-Pool Soil Carbon

  • Tracks aboveground and belowground residue carbon inputs.
  • Runs parallel AMGv2, RothC, and measurable Millennial (POM / MAOM) carbon dynamics.
  • Accounts for lateral erosional carbon export.
  • Applies forward-mode automatic differentiation and knowledge-guided mass-conservation gates.

⑤ 💰 Complete Farm Economics & “What Should I Plant?” Advisor

The advisor (#/plant) compares rotations across identical climate years, using:

  • Three non-overlapping financial accounts: Gross Margin, Net Accounting Result, and Multi-Year Cash Flow.
  • Detailed production ledgers: Eight input-cost rubrics and N-P-K-S nutrients.
  • Common-horizon investment metrics: Net Present Value (NPV) and Equivalent Annuity (AE).
  • Mixed crop-livestock accounting: Forage-to-beef livestock budgets.
  • Non-additive soil-degradation valuation.
  • Tail-loss assessment: Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR).
  • Exact crop-price tipping points.

⑥ 🎯 Multi-Objective Search, Honest Abstention & Value of Information

The platform explores alternatives and identifies where additional evidence could change a decision:

  • Constrained NSGA-II Pareto optimization: Searches thousands of candidate rotations.
  • PRIM scenario discovery: Identifies vulnerability thresholds.
  • DAPP adaptive pathways: Builds trigger-based strategies.
  • Pairwise robustness assessment: Classifies comparisons as 🟢 Robust, 🟡 Conditional, or ⚪ Unresolved.

When uncertainty prevents a safe choice, the system:

  • Abstains from guessing.
  • Quantifies the Expected Value of Perfect Information (EVPI) and Expected Value of Sample Information (EVSI) in USD per hectare.
  • Tells the farmer what to measure first in the field.
  • Exports a grounded, hallucination-checked printable field decision sheet (#/print).

🔎 Scientific Validity & Four-Axis Governance

Every capability in the 46-line technical registry tracks four independent axes:

  • Method Maturity
  • Implementation Status
  • Data Availability
  • Local Validation Status

This separates established literature equations from locally validated field predictions.

All engines apply:

  • Mass-balance closure.
  • Simple baseline comparators.
  • Pre-registered benchmarks against published references and runoff plots in Colonia, Uruguay.
  • Layer-ablation checks, pruning any layer that fails to narrow decision uncertainty.
  • Typed missing-value propagation, ensuring unmeasured inputs are never silently replaced by zero.

🏛️ Local & Global Impact: Automating Farm Plans and National Public Compliance

🇺🇾 For Uruguayan Farmers & Agronomists

Automates preparation and stress-testing for Uruguay’s mandatory Soil Use and Management Plans, covering 1.65 million hectares—nearly 96% of national rainfed cropland.

The platform turns a static paperwork obligation into a dynamic tool that protects topsoil and multi-year farm cash flow.

🌐 For Government Regulators

Pairs full-physics simulation with a physics-informed neural grid emulator, requiring full-physics recalculation for all finalist solutions.

Public agencies can:

  • Audit watershed compliance consistently.
  • Stress-test national conservation standards against 2030–2060 climate scenarios.

🌾 Global Scalability

Global NASA Earth observations and modular soil and economic interfaces allow rainfed farming regions worldwide to deploy the twin and adapt to intensifying climate extremes.

🛠️ Tools, Software & Responsible Use of Super Intelligence

Open-source license: Apache-2.0

Backend & Infrastructure

  • Python, FastAPI, Pydantic, HTTPX, and Uvicorn.
  • Docker and cloud container infrastructure.

Frontend & Mapping

  • TypeScript, React, Vite, and Tailwind CSS.
  • Leaflet and OpenStreetMap.

Testing & Delivery

  • Vitest.
  • Automated seven-gate continuous-integration pipelines.
  • GitHub Pages.

At runtime: Outputs are governed by deterministic physical, statistical, optimization, and economic formulations, with numeric grounding verification and no unconstrained text generation.

During development: The team used AI coding and research assistants under human architectural direction, with human verification of scientific parameters and citations.
